metaTitle: Mesne Profits for Illegal Land Occupation Bangladesh
title: Mesne Profits for Illegal Land Occupation Bangladesh
metaDescription: Claim financial compensation (Mesne Profits) from a trespasser or holdover tenant in Bangladesh under Section 2(12) and Order 20 Rule 12 CPC 1908.
keywords: Section 2(12) Code of Civil Procedure Bangladesh
heroIntro: Under Section 2(12) and Order 20 Rule 12 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a lawful landowner in Bangladesh can recover 'Mesne Profits'—the fair rental value and profits actually received or reasonably obtainable during wrongful possession, plus interest—alongside eviction of a trespasser or holdover tenant after lease termination.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Mesne Profits Law in Bangladesh
points: Governing Law: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Section 2(12) & Order 20 Rule 12; Limitation Act, 1908 — Article 109 (3 years).
Limitation Window: You can claim past mesne profits for up to 3 years prior to filing the suit (Article 109), plus future profits until eviction.
Calculation Basis: Fair market rental value of the property (not the trespasser's personal business losses), plus interest.
Forum: Assistant Judge, Senior Assistant Judge, or Joint District Judge Court combined with a possession recovery suit.

sections.h2: What Are Mesne Profits Under Section 2(12) CPC?
sections.content:
Section 2(12) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 defines mesne profits (pronounced 'mean profits') as those profits which a person in wrongful possession of property actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received therefrom, together with interest on such profits, but excluding profits due to improvements made by the person in wrongful possession.

In practical terms, if a squatter, former caretaker, or holdover tenant whose lease has been validly terminated refuses to vacate your house, shop, or agricultural land, simply getting them evicted years later does not compensate you for lost rental income. Mesne profits ensure the wrongful occupant pays the fair market rental value for the entire period of illegal occupation.

Always include an explicit prayer for mesne profits in your possession recovery suit; consult a property litigation lawyer in Bangladesh before filing so you do not waive past claims.

sections.h2: Who Is Liable to Pay Mesne Profits in Bangladesh?
sections.content:
Liability for mesne profits depends strictly on whether the occupant's possession was wrongful during the claimed period, rather than permissive or lawful under an active contract.

Occupant CategoryWhen Possession Becomes WrongfulMesne Profits Liability
Trespasser / Land GrabberFrom day one of unlawful entry or dispossession.Liable for full market rental/crop value up to 3 years pre-suit + pendente lite.
Holdover TenantAfter expiry of lease or valid Section 106 TP Act termination notice.Liable for fair market rent (often higher than old contractual rent) post-notice.
Co-Sharer in Joint PropertyOnly after proven ouster/exclusion of other co-sharers.Normally accounted in partition decree rather than trespass damages.
Permissive Caretaker / LicenseeFrom the date written revocation notice expires.Liable from expiry of notice period until actual delivery of vacant possession.

If an encroacher has occupied NRB land for years, review our 12-year adverse possession defence guide to act before limitation expires.

sections.h2: How Courts Calculate Mesne Profits and the 3-Year Limitation Rule
sections.content:
Under Article 109 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908, a suit for the profits of immovable property belonging to the plaintiff which have been wrongfully received by the defendant must be filed within 3 years from when the profits are received. Consequently, while you can recover possession within 12 years, past mesne profits are capped at the 3 years immediately preceding the filing of the plaint.

However, under Order 20 Rule 12(1)(c) CPC, the court may also direct an inquiry into future mesne profits accruing from the institution of the suit until delivery of possession to the decree-holder, or the expiration of three years from the date of the decree, whichever occurs first. Courts measure mesne profits by what an ordinary prudent owner could have earned in rent—established through neighbouring lease deeds, mouza agricultural yield rates, or an Advocate Commissioner's local inquiry report—rather than what the trespasser claims they earned.

Note that under Section 11 of the Court-Fees Act, 1870, when the exact amount of future mesne profits is ascertained in the final decree, the plaintiff must pay the balance ad valorem court fee before executing the monetary recovery.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Procedure to Claim Mesne Profits in a Possession Suit
sections.content:
Follow this two-stage civil court procedure under Order 20 Rule 12 CPC to recover both your land and accumulated rental damages:

  1. Serve Revocation / Termination Notice: If the occupant entered as a tenant or caretaker, serve a formal written notice revoking permission or terminating tenancy under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 to fix the start date of wrongful possession.
  2. Include Past & Future Mesne Profits in the Plaint: Pray for (a) recovery of khas possession, (b) ascertained past mesne profits for up to 3 years pre-suit (paying tentative court fee under Section 7(i)/(ii) Court-Fees Act), and (c) an Order 20 Rule 12 inquiry for pendente lite and future mesne profits.
  3. Secure Preliminary Possession Decree: At trial, prove title, wrongful possession, and comparable market rent in the locality.
  4. Conduct Order 20 Rule 12 Inquiry: After winning possession, apply for an Advocate Commissioner or court inquiry to assess exact monthly rent, seasonal crop yield, and statutory interest.
  5. Pay Balance Court Fee & Execute Final Decree: Pay any balance court fee under Section 11 of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 and execute the money decree via property attachment or bank garnishment; Advocate Md. Shah Alam represents resident and NRB owners in full possession and mesne-profit recoveries.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for Proving Mesne Profits
sections.content:
Gather these valuation and title records so the court awards realistic market rates rather than nominal sums:

  • Registered title deed, Khatian (CS/SA/RS/BS), and Mutation records proving ownership.
  • Written termination/eviction notice and postal/courier delivery receipts fixing the date possession became wrongful.
  • Comparable local lease deeds, commercial rent receipts, or municipal holding valuation sheets showing fair market rent.
  • Prior tenancy agreement (for holdover tenants) or agricultural yield estimates (for farmland).
  • For NRBs abroad: an Embassy-attested Power of Attorney authorising local representation.

Also review Order 40 Receiver remedies for active commercial rentals, visit our NRB Legal Help Desk, or book a free initial consultation.

faqs.question: Can I file a separate lawsuit later for mesne profits if I forgot to claim them in my eviction suit?
faqs.answer: Under Order 2 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, past mesne profits accrued before the suit can be claimed either together with possession or separately within the 3-year limit (Article 109). However, future mesne profits accruing during the suit must be prayed for in the possession suit itself under Order 20 Rule 12.

faqs.question: How many years of past mesne profits can I recover in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Article 109 of the Limitation Act, 1908, you can recover past mesne profits for a maximum of 3 years immediately preceding the date of filing your lawsuit, plus future mesne profits from the filing date until delivery of possession (or 3 years post-decree).

faqs.question: Can a trespasser deduct money they spent building a structure on my land?
faqs.answer: No. Section 2(12) CPC explicitly excludes profits due to improvements made by the person in wrongful possession. While a trespasser cannot charge the owner for unauthorised buildings, mesne profits are calculated on the unimproved market rental value of the owner's property.

faqs.question: Are mesne profits awarded with interest in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 2(12) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 expressly defines mesne profits as including 'together with interest on such profits'. Civil courts routinely award simple interest (commonly 6% per annum under Section 34 CPC) on unpaid monthly mesne profits.

faqs.question: What if a tenant stays after the lease expires and keeps paying old rent?
faqs.answer: If the landlord accepts old rent after expiry without protest, a statutory holding-over tenancy under Section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act may arise. To claim higher market mesne profits, the landlord should refuse rent after valid notice or accept payments strictly 'without prejudice' as damages for use and occupation.
